newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tractebel stars on Belgian share market.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel stars on Belgian share market.

text.p: Utility holding company Tractebel was the star of the Belgian share market on Wednesday, climbing more than six percent to a premium of 500 francs above the 14,500 franc offer price from Societe General de Belgique (SGB).

SGB, Belgium's biggest holding company, announced late on Tuesday it had agreed to raise its stake in Tractebel to 65 percent from 40 and extend the offer to the remaining 35 percent at a price of 14,500 per share. It also offered shareholders a free put warrant, exercisable at 14,500 francs in three years. Traders said this was the price-boosting factor.
"Tractebel is being boosted by the put warrant," one trader said. "We believe people will keep on buying the stock."
Estimates of the fair price of the warrant varied between 1,100 and 1,600 francs on top of the 14,500 franc guaranteed price.
Traders noted that more than 65,000 shares had changed hands in hectic morning trading in Tractebel.

SGB bought the 25 percent chunk of Tractebel on Tuesday from holding company Electrafina and insurer Royale Belge for a total price of 49 billion francs of which 41 billion goes to Electrafina and eight billion to Royale Belge.
In both cases, roughly half the amount was capital gain.
Electrafina duly rose 20 francs to 2,870, and Royale Belge climbed 70 francs to 6,000.
However, traders warned that the Royale Belge gains were unlikely to be sustainable due to the adverse impact of its upcoming reweighting in the Bel-20 share index on Friday.
SGB and Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL), the company that has stakes in both Electrafina and Royale Belge, barely reacted to the announcement of the tractebel deal.
SGB edged up 15 francs to 2,555, while GBL added 30 francs to 3,875.
Traders also noted that Powerfin, a unit of Tractebel, was very active -- falling 1.3 percent to 4,720 francs on a volume of 30,000 shares in anticipation of people reshuffling their portfolios.
Kredietbank continued its steady climb, rising 0.7 percent to 10,575 francs. Traders said they expected the price to move still higher.

Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere, which on Tuesday reported a 30 percent drop in group net profit for the first half of 1995, fell 10 francs to 2,370 on market disappointment despite forecasts for improvement in the second half.
Traders said the UM share decline was muted by the positive effects of its reweighting on Friday in the BEL-20.
The index was 6.76 points up at 1,762.91 at 1000 GMT, in the middle of a 1,765.97/1,760.27 range. There were 12 gainers, one unchanged and seven losers.
Total market volume was a healthy two billion francs, of which 1.7 billion francs were in shares in the index.
